41637-the-forgotten-planet.creator: Unknown

arxiv-1904-11887.creator: Tamás Erdélyi
arxiv-1904-11887.description:
A 2019 arXiv research paper by Tamás Erdélyi. We give a simple, elementary, and at least partially new proof of Arestov’s famous extension of Bernstein’s inequality in L p L_{p} to all p ≥ 0 p\geq 0 . arxiv-2012-07799.title: Rate-dependent adhesion of viscoelastic contacts. Part II: numerical model and hysteresis dissipation
arxiv-2012-07799.creator: G. Violano, A. Chateauminois, L. Afferrante
arxiv-2012-07799.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a numerical model to describe the adhesive normal contact between a ‘rigid’ spherical indenter and a viscoelastic rough substrate. The model accounts for dissipative process under the assumption that viscoelastic losses are localized at the (micro)-contact lines.

arxiv-2203-10579.title: Small Batch Sizes Improve Training of Low-Resource Neural MT
arxiv-2203-10579.creator: Àlex R. Atrio 1,2 and Andrei Popescu-Belis 1,2 1 HEIG-VD / HES-SO 2 EPFL Yverdon-les-Bains Lausanne Switzerland Switzerland {alejandro.ramirezatrio, andrei.popescu-belis}@heig-vd.ch
arxiv-2203-10579.description: Abstract We study the role of an essential hyper-parameter that governs the training of Transformers for neural machine translation in a low-resource setting: the batch size. Using theoretical insights and experimental evidence, we argue against the widespread belief that batch size should be set as large as allowed by the memory of the GPUs.

arxiv-2303-06160.title: Modified Villain formulation of abelian Chern-Simons theory
arxiv-2303-06160.creator: Theodore Jacobson, Tin Sulejmanpasic
arxiv-2303-06160.description: Abstract We formulate U ​ ( 1 ) k U(1)_{k} Chern-Simons theory on a Euclidean spacetime lattice using the modified Villain approach. Various familiar aspects of continuum Chern-Simons theory such as level quantization, framing, the discrete 1-form symmetry and its ’t Hooft anomaly, as well as the electric charge of monopole operators are manifest in our construction.

arxiv-2309-10792.title: Frequentist Inference for Semi-mechanistic Epidemic Models with Interventions
arxiv-2309-10792.creator: Heejong Bong, Valérie Ventura, Larry Wasserman
arxiv-2309-10792.description: Abstract The effect of public health interventions on an epidemic are often estimated by adding the intervention to epidemic models. During the Covid-19 epidemic, numerous papers used such methods for making scenario predictions. The majority of these papers use Bayesian methods to estimate the parameters of the model.

arxiv-2402-11382.title: Secure, Robust, and Energy-Efficient Authenticated Data Sharing in UAV-Assisted 6G Networks
arxiv-2402-11382.creator: Atefeh Mohseni Ejiyeh
arxiv-2402-11382.description: Abstract This paper confronts the pressing challenges of sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication networks by harnessing the unique capabilities of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). With the ambitious promises of 6G, including ultra-reliable 1 Tbps data delivery and ultra-low latency, the demand for innovative solutions becomes imperative.

arxiv-2404-14404.title: Multipolar Skyrmion Crystals in Non-Kramers Doublet Systems
arxiv-2404-14404.creator: Hao Zhang, Shi-Zeng Lin
arxiv-2404-14404.description: Abstract We study the Kondo lattice model of multipolar magnetic moments interacting with conduction electrons on a triangular lattice. Bond-dependent electron hoppings induce a compass-like anisotropy in the effective Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida interaction between multipolar moments. This unique anisotropy stabilizes multipolar skyrmion crystals with a skyrmion topological charge of 1 and 2 at a zero magnetic field.

arxiv-2509-12482.title: Towards Foundational Models for Single-Chip Radar
arxiv-2509-12482.creator: Tianshu Huang Akarsh Prabhakara Chuhan Chen Jay Karhade, Deva Ramanan Matthew O’Toole Anthony Rowe
arxiv-2509-12482.description: Abstract mmWave radars are compact, inexpensive, and durable sensors that are robust to occlusions and work regardless of environmental conditions, such as weather and darkness. However, this comes at the cost of poor angular resolution, especially for inexpensive single-chip radars, which are typically used in automotive and indoor sensing applications.

britannica-1911-peter-lombard.description: Article 'Peter Lombard' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 21), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born about the beginning of the 12th century, at Novara (then reckoned as belonging to Lombardy). After receiving his education at Bologna, he removed to France, bearing a recommendation to Bernard of Clairvaux, who first placed him under Lotolf at Reims, and afterwards sent him to Paris with letters to Gilduin, the abbot of St Victor.

pmc-10559545.title: Comparison of the Retention and Fit of Polyether Ether Ketone Clasps during Fatigue Circulation Tests☆
pmc-10559545.creator: Su Wu, Chao Qian, Ting Jiao, Jian Sun
pmc-10559545.description: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to evaluate the fit and retention of clasps made of polyether ether ketone (PEEK) or cobalt–chromium alloy (Co–Cr) at different tooth positions in experimental simulations of in vitro wear and removal for 5 years.

pmc-11531234.title: The Role of Nitric Oxide, Lipocalin-2, and Proinflammatory Cytokines on Proteinuria and Insulin Resistance in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Subgroups
pmc-11531234.creator: Chung Hyun Nahm, Moon Hee Lee, Noriyoshi Fujii, Tatsuyoshi Fujii, Jong Weon Choi
pmc-11531234.description: BackgroundNitric oxide (NO) is a bioactive signaling molecule that mediates various physiological and biological processes. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) can be categorized into several subgroups according to fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels. Few studies have closely examined the effect of NO and lipocalin-2 on albuminuria and insulin resistance in T2DM subgroups.

pmc-12374391.title: Using the R = MC2 heuristic to assess whole-of-school physical activity implementation in elementary schools: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12374391.creator: Derek W Craig, Kevin Lanza, Christopher D Pfledderer, Andjelka Pavlovic, Kempson Onadeko, Natalia I Heredia, Jizyah Injil, Laura F DeFina, Timothy J Walker
pmc-12374391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundSchools are recommended to use a whole-of-school (WOS) approach to promote physical activity opportunities before, during, and after school. Yet, the barriers and facilitators to implementing a WOS approach successfully are not well understood. The R = MC2 heuristic, which defines readiness for implementation as a combination of an organization’s motivation and capacity to implement, can enhance our understanding of implementation in the school setting.

pmc-12509919.title: Metabolic Syndrome-Associated Erectile Dysfunction: Multiple Vascular Endothelial Dysfunction Mechanisms and Potential Therapeutic Targets
pmc-12509919.creator: Hao Wang, Jun Guo, Eric Chung
pmc-12509919.description: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) causes vascular structural abnormalities, nerve damage, hormonal level changes and other lesions, which promote the occurrence and development of erectile dysfunction (ED). Penile vascular endothelial dysfunction is an important pathological feature of MetS-associated ED, and has received increasing attention in recent years.

pmc-12535435.title: A Case Report of Autoimmune Gastritis Associated With Polyendocrine Syndrome Type III Mimicking Refractory H. pylori Infection
pmc-12535435.creator: Saki Ubukata, Hideki Mori, Tatsuhiro Masaoka, Juntaro Matsuzaki, Takanori Kanai
pmc-12535435.description: A 60-year-old woman had persistent positive urea breath test (UBT) results despite three courses of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) eradication therapy. Endoscopy revealed extensive atrophic gastritis with a characteristic "reverse atrophic pattern" affecting the gastric corpus while sparing the antrum. Active H. pylori infection was excluded; however, positivity for anti-parietal cell and anti-intrinsic factor antibodies confirmed autoimmune gastritis (AIG).

pmc-12737178.title: Recent Advances in Membrane-Based Air Filtration Technologies for Ambient Particulate Matter Separation
pmc-12737178.creator: Prarthana Bora, Chinmoy Bhuyan, Duraikkanu Shanthana Lakshmi, Swapnali Hazarika, Marek Tanczyk, Srinivas T G Srimath, Jonghak Kim
pmc-12737178.description: Varied types of particulate matter (PM) persist in the environment and exert a harmful impact on public health. The aim of this review article is to explore the key role of membrane technology in the separation of PM from ambient air. Nanofibrous, microporous, Janus, photocatalytic and hollow fiber membranes have found significant utilization in the effective separation of PM.

pmc-13000486.title: Preliminary results of 3D MRI-DSA fusion for navigation planning in endovascular recanalization of chronic intracranial artery occlusion
pmc-13000486.creator: Yi Quan, Su-shan Hu, Fang Liu, Ji Zhou, Qi Sun, Min Jin, Chen Li, Ao-fei Liu
pmc-13000486.description: BackgroundChronic intracranial artery occlusion (CIAO) is a critical non-acute manifestaticon within the spectrum of intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD). In Asian populations, ICAD is common and remains associated with substantial recurrent ischemic risk despite best medical therapy, making endovascular recanalization an important but technically challenging intervention due to the limitations of conventional 2D DSA guidance.

pmc-13016746.title: Is Burn Center Admission Necessary After Home Oxygen Ignition Injury?
pmc-13016746.creator: Hope E Werenski, Anju Saraswat, James H Holmes, John K Bailey
pmc-13016746.description: Accidental ignition of home oxygen does not mandate emergent intubation, but due to the thermal component of the injury, patients are initially directed toward burn units. To identify potential benefit associated with admission to an American Burn Association (ABA)-verified burn center, the local registry was queried from January 2016 to May 2022.

pmc-13137524.title: Exosomal lncRNA DLEU2 aggravates inflammatory injury and apoptosis in pediatric viral pneumonia via the miR-330-5p
pmc-13137524.creator: Xinxing Su, Haobin Wang, Jianzhu He, Huagui Bai
pmc-13137524.description: BackgroundViral pneumonia (VP) is a major cause of severe respiratory illness in children. lncRNAs are involved in disease progression by regulating immune regulation. This study investigates the clinical value and regulatory function of exosomal DLEU2 in pediatric VP.MaterialsInclude 247 pediatric VP cases, divided into 120 mild and 127 severe groups, and collected plasma exosomes samples.

pmc-13419848.title: Fellowship Training Trends Among Spine Neurosurgeons in Florida: A Cross-Sectional Analysis
pmc-13419848.creator: Maria Fioletova, Umangpreet Gill, Alexandra Lugo, Evelyn C Echevarria Cruz, Julieanne P Sees
pmc-13419848.description: Introduction: Neurosurgical fellowships to obtain additional surgical training after residency are a career option widely available to the newer generation of neurosurgeons. This study aims to analyze current trends in fellowship training among spine neurosurgeons in Florida and factors that influence the choice of fellowship based on year, location, and academic trajectory.

pmc-13451321.title: Microbiota awareness and fermented food consumption among university students: evidence of a knowledge-behavior gap
pmc-13451321.creator: Ayşe Nur Kahve, Hande Yazıcıoğlu Çalışan
pmc-13451321.description: Fermented foods are traditional functional foods that may beneficially influence gut microbiota composition and contribute to overall health. However, it remains unclear whether microbiota-related awareness is associated with regular consumption of fermented foods. This study aimed to examine the association between microbiota awareness and fermented food consumption among university students.

pmc-13572967.title: Next‐Generation Manufacturing: The Evolving Role of Biocatalysis in AstraZeneca
pmc-13572967.creator: Alba Diaz‐Rodriguez, Martin A Hayes, Keith R Mulholland, Fernando Tur, Samantha Staniland
pmc-13572967.description: Biocatalysis is becoming a strategic manufacturing capability at AstraZeneca, enabling selective transformations under milder conditions and with the potential to reduce waste and resource intensity relative to conventional routes. This review summarizes how AstraZeneca is embedding biocatalysis across the portfolio to support its long‐term net‐zero commitments.

pmc-13668899.title: Refining risk prediction in geriatric heart failure: the emergency heart failure mortality risk grade‑BI model under scrutiny
pmc-13668899.creator: Kianoush A. h. Saberi L., Durdona Alimova, Sherzod Niyazov, Kholmurod Qayumov, Parvina Gaffarova, Xamida Juraqobilova, Zaynura Kadirova
pmc-13668899.description: Risk stratification is critical for managing acute heart failure in older adults, yet existing tools often underperform in geriatric populations. Özdemir recently introduced the EHMRG‑BI model, integrating brain natriuretic peptide and endotracheal intubation with the Emergency Heart Failure Mortality Risk Grade score to improve 30‑day mortality prediction.
